turns.content: A cyclohexanone precursor forms the specified fused enone under NaOH, water, and heat. Identify the required sequence of intramolecular Michael addition followed by intramolecular aldol condensation, using a C5-tethered conjugated enone.
Infer the precursor stereochemistry needed to give the product's stated methyl/ethyl relationship, and identify the incompatible relationship.
Describe the ring-closure and atom-mapping method used to work backward from the fused target.
Use the target topology to locate the side-chain attachment on the cyclohexanone ring.
Determine the tether functionality, alkene geometry, and carbonyl placement required by the reaction sequence established above.
Trace the bond-forming events and intermediates through the sequence established above to the target.
Identify precursor X by full stereochemical name and justify its stereochemistry, tether position, and reactivity.
Check the proposed stereocentres, attachment point, alkene geometry, and carbonyl position against every step of the intramolecular Michael-addition/aldol cascade.
Report X with a concise mapping based on the reaction sequence established above.
